{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past purchases as continuing interest in broadly related products, with insufficient distinction between general affinity and a current reason to choose.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Direct artist connections, repeated interests, and close matches to recent viewing or listening preferences produce convincing recommendations.",
    "Complementary supplies and devices align well when they support an established task or add a useful capability to existing equipment."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broad topical similarity competes too strongly with specific task, mood, artist, and compatibility matches.",
    "Recent purchases are treated as reasons to recommend similar products without sufficiently accounting for needs those purchases have already satisfied.",
    "Historical interests are carried forward without enough sensitivity to current priorities, seasonal context, or the age of the interaction."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared product domains, device ecosystems, broad genres, and album formats appear to substitute for a concrete connection to the user's intent.",
    "Interest in one tool, accessory, or device is extended to adjacent tasks and equipment whose relevance is unsupported by the history."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent and repeated specific interests provide stronger choice signals than isolated or broadly related past interactions.",
    "Compatibility, dimensions, quantities, required equipment, and incremental usefulness determine whether a related product is actionable.",
    "Specific artist relationships, mood, musical delivery, and task continuity distinguish compelling matches from superficial similarity.",
    "Insufficient item information leaves relevance uncertain; such uncertainty should not be interpreted as demonstrated dislike."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Broadly plausible items occupy leading ranks despite lacking the specific current purpose, content connection, or added usefulness that would make users choose them now.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked items users would choose now, separated from items they consider merely related or potentially useful later.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to duplicated functionality, incompatible specifications, excessive quantities, or unsupported task assumptions.",
    "The ranking positions of recommendations with direct recent-interest connections compared with recommendations supported only by broad similarity.",
    "The proportion of recommendation judgments that remain uncertain because item content or compatibility cannot be established."
  ]
}
